title.narrative: IJR, 2017-2021, Core Support - IJR core support 2017-2020

description.narrative: In 2017, IJR will rework their overall Results Framework in order to establish consistent and logical linkages between the intended outcomes (goals), their indicators and main activities. The overriding expected outcomes - as defined in IJR's Strategic Plan - will obviously constitute the point of departure in this context. These outcomes are: (1) Advancement of regional reconciliation as a concept and in practice (2) Increased application of transitional and victim-centred justice and reconciliation (3) Establishing bottom-up reconciliation and restoration of human dignity as a key approach (4) Reduce racism, increase social cohesion and inclusion (5) Improve socio-economic justice in South Africa

The Institute for Justice and Reconciliation (IJR) is a not-for profit think tank with headquarters in Cape Town, South Africa. The main purpose of IJR is to contribute to reconciliation and social justice in Africa. IJR was born directly out of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission which played an important role during the transition from apartheid to democracy in South Africa. The country's former arch bishop, Desmond Tutu, is the patron of IJR and still contributes actively. IJR has received Swedish core support since 2007 and has been the subject of several evaluations (the latest one in 2015) - all of them showing good results.
IJR's Strategic Plan for 2017-2020 focuses on: - Regional reconciliation - Transitional and victim-centred justice - Restoring human dignity - Bottom-up reconciliation - Racism, social cohesion and inclusion - Socio-economic justice. In addition, IJR also emphasizes Gender and Youth as two cross-cutting themes.
IJR collaborates with international, continental and sub-regional organizations in order to achieve the key aspects of SDG 16 related to peace and security for sustainable development. The organization also works directly with governments and civil society in seven African countries (South Sudan, Burundi, eastern Congo, Uganda, Rwanda, Kenya and Zimbabwe) and also undertakes active work at grass-roots level in South Africa.
IJR utilizes applied research and analysis as support for policy development and advisory services.
IJR’s Theory of Change states that if the Institute engages with policy and decision makers, supports capacity development and reinforces community-led reconciliation, then stakeholders (policy and key decision makers, CSOs, youth, academia etc) will acquire and develop the necessary skills and knowledge to promote transitional justice and reconciliation in their own countries and regions.
The proposed Swedish support covers a period of 4 years (2017-2020) and amounts to a total of SEK 28 million.
